objects.name: Fiber Section (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Collects fibre points, layers and patches into one section.
The green y and blue z arrows are the section's local axes: y along world X, z along world Y, the way OpenSees writes a fibre. They are drawn at the area centroid of the fibres, the point moments are taken about. My and Mz - in Moment Curvature, Interaction Domain and its views - are moments about y and z by the right-hand rule, the beam's axis x coming out of the drawing (towards you in Top view): positive My stretches the +z side, positive Mz the -y side.

objects.name: MomentCurvature (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Pushes a fibre section's curvature in any moment direction under a held axial force, and returns the moment-curvature curve, the stress-strain history of every fibre, and the curve's first yield and ultimate state.
The ultimate state is the first fibre at its ultimate strain - Interaction Domain's limits: concrete at εcu, or εc2 at point C in full compression, everything else at εud - and the analysis stops there unless told not to.

objects.name: Interaction Domain (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
The N-My-Mz resistance domain of a fibre section at the ultimate limit state: every combination of axial force and biaxial bending it carries before a fibre passes its material's ultimate strain.
OpenSees traces each material's stress-strain curve; the ultimate strain planes are then swept through the section the way Eurocode 2 6.1 pivots them - concrete at εcu, or εc2 at point C in full compression, everything else at εud.
Moments are about the area centroid of the fibres, as Moment Curvature's are.

objects.name: N-M Diagram (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Draws the N-M interaction diagram of a domain: its cut by the plane that holds the N axis and the moment direction Angle - 0° for N-My, 90° for N-Mz. M along the plane's X, N along its Y with compression up.
The Checks of a Domain Check are drawn projected onto the cut: exactly on it only when their moment points along Angle.

objects.desc: Draws moment-curvature curves: κ along the plane's X, M along its Y, scaled to fit Size, with each curve's first yield in orange and its ultimate state in red. Wire several Moment Curvature results to compare them - at different axial forces, say.

objects.desc:
Draws the My-Mz interaction diagram of a domain at each axial force N: My along the plane's X, Mz along its Y, to one scale for both.
The Checks of a Domain Check are drawn by their moments, whatever their N.

objects.name: Panel
objects.desc: A panel for custom notes and text values
objects.text:
HEA 300 in fibres - a rolled steel section under three laws.

Two flanges (300 x 14) and a web (8.5 x 262), the root radii left out, meshed in 600 fibres each way, S355. Moment Curvature bends it about the strong axis, Direction 0, without axial force, in Steel02 (smooth knee, 1 % hardening), Steel01 (sharp knee, 1 %) and a Hysteretic backbone rising to 1.15 fy; the last row bends Steel02 about the weak axis, Direction 90. The curves show the plastic reserve: the ultimate moment against the moment at first yield. Every law here hardens: a perfectly plastic one (ElasticPP) leaves a bare section with no stiffness once it is fully yielded, and the analysis cannot go on.

The N-M diagrams are cut along My; the My-Mz diagram is the first law's domain at N = 0 and at 1000 kN of compression.

Try: Direction between 0 and 90; Axial from 0 to -2000; the steel strength in the Steel components.
